title: Console feature slice: Phase 1 dashboard + tracing + route-level cost MVP
creator: Aisha Karim
description: Context: The Console Observability v2 PRD is too large for the Q1 milestone. This ticket defines the Phase 1 (MVP) scope cuts and acceptance criteria for dashboards, tracing surface, and cost breakdown so engineering can begin an implementation that delivers clear value while deferring lower-priority work.
scope_changes: 1) Dashboards: deliver a single configurable overview page limited to 3 cards: Aggregate latency by route, error-rate by route, and throughput (RPS) across selected time windows. Remove ad-hoc secondary cards (token-level cost, model-level distribution) from MVP. 2) Tracing: expose a sampled span view that links from the error-rate card to top 20 recent traces for a route. No span-level search or custom sampling policies in Phase 1. 3) Cost breakdown: provide route-level aggregated cost estimates (USD/day and tokens/day) with simple filters by time range and model family. Defer token-level per-call breakdown, budget alerts, and chargeback export until Phase 2.
acceptance_criteria:
- Dashboard overview page exists and can be opened from Console nav.
- Three cards render within 3s for accounts up to 100k requests/day.
- Cards are configurable: time range (1h/24h/7d) and route filter.
- Error-rate card links to a tracing view and shows top failing routes.
- Tracing view returns top 20 captured traces for a route within 5s for common workloads.
- Cost breakdown displays route-level USD/day and tokens/day with time range selector and a CSV download of the aggregated route rows.
- Feature flags exist to toggle each surface per org.
- Automated E2E smoke test validates dashboard load and trace link for a synthetic route.
- Docs/Console help updated with MVP limitations and roadmap notes.
- Performance budgets observed in staging (95th percentile render latency < 3s).
decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Trade-off: We prioritize time-to-value and reliability over breadth. Token-level cost is high engineering effort with marginal early ROI; we defer it.
- Decision: Sampling-based tracing only for MVP to reduce storage and query complexity. Full span-indexing and search moved to Phase 2.
- Trade-off: Limiting to 3 cards keeps frontend engineering scope manageable and reduces backend telemetry queries. Complex drilldowns will be added later.
- Decision: Route-level cost uses aggregated meter readings and estimation heuristics instead of exact per-call attribution to avoid adding a high-cardinality join in the billing pipeline. This will be documented in the UI as "estimated" and revisited post-MVP.
- Risk: Some enterprise customers expect token-level chargeback; we'll communicate roadmap and offer Dedicated customers an early opt-in beta via support tickets.
progress_updates:
2025-02-10: Drafted initial scope cuts after PM/Eng sync; flagged token-level cost as deferred.
2025-02-14: Design provided wireframes for 3-card dashboard (DES-1182).
2025-02-20: Engineering scoped backend changes for aggregated cost rows; estimated 8 story points (ENG-9214).
2025-02-25: Security reviewed data surface and confirmed no additional PII is surfaced.
2025-03-01: UX review: clarified trace view should show timestamp, duration, error flag, and a short call-stack snippet.
2025-03-04: PM sign-off on scope; moved ticket to Planned and added feature flags and QA checklist.
qa_checklist:
- Verify nav link and page loads in staging orgs with synthetic traffic.
- Validate 3 cards render and update when time-range or route filter changes.
- Confirm error-rate card links to tracing view and the trace list contains at most 20 items sorted by recency.
- Run load test for an org with 100k requests/day to confirm 95p dashboard render latency < 3s.
- Ensure CSV download includes route, tokens/day, usd/day, and time window.
- Confirm feature flags disable the surfaces completely when turned off.
- Validate docs page explains estimation methodology for route-level cost.
- Verify E2E smoke test passes in CI with synthetic traffic generator.
